sources.locator: CS2023 Algorithmic Foundations; August 2023; material applicable to Union by rank or size
sources.claim: Union by rank or size attaches the shallower or smaller tree beneath the larger representative to limit height.

canonicalExplanation.summary: Plain union can build a long chain, making find O(n). **Union by rank** keeps trees short: each root stores a **rank**, an upper bound on its tree's height. When joining two roots, attach the **lower-rank** root **under the higher-rank** one; the height doesn't grow. Only when the ranks are **equal** do you pick either as the new root and **increase its rank by 1**. **Union by size** does the same with member counts: the smaller tree goes under the larger. Either way, tree height stays **O(log n)**, so find is O(log n) even before path compression.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A platform merges learners into study groups one pair at a time, always attaching the old group under the newest learner. After 10,000 merges, checking whether two learners share a group walks a chain thousands of links long. Equal-rank roots are joined and the chosen new root's rank increases once. In this lesson you'll implement and trace union by rank or size while preserving representatives.

```predict
{"question": "Root A has rank 3, root B has rank 1. Which goes under which?", "options": ["A under B", "B under A: the lower rank joins the higher"], "answer": 1, "why": "Hanging the short tree under the tall one keeps the height at 3."}
```

examples.title: Keeping study-group trees short
examples.situation: Equal-rank roots are joined and the chosen new root's rank increases once.
walkthrough: **Singletons:** union(0, 1) joins two rank-0 roots; 0 becomes the root and its rank rises to 1.
**Unequal ranks:** union(0, 2) puts rank-0 root 2 under rank-1 root 0, and the rank stays 1.
**Equal again:** union of two rank-1 groups makes one root rank 2; a test will check heights never exceed log2 of the group size.
examples.result: Membership checks stay fast after thousands of merges, because trees stay short.

examples.title: The chain built by always attaching left
examples.situation: A union that always sets parent[root(x)] = root(y) is given pairs (0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), ... up to 9,999. find(0) walks 9,999 links.
walkthrough: Each union put the whole existing tree under a new single item.
With union by rank, each new singleton (rank 0) goes under the big tree's root.
The tree stays height 1 for this sequence.
examples.result: find(0) takes one step instead of thousands.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Union by rank attaches the larger-rank root under the smaller one.
misconceptions.correction: It's the opposite: the lower-rank (shorter) tree is attached under the higher-rank root, so the combined height doesn't grow. Height grows only when two equal ranks meet.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, which root stayed on top?

analogy.example: Union by rank is like **merging two companies' org charts**: you place the smaller chart under the bigger company's CEO, so the chain of command doesn't get deeper. Only when two equally deep charts merge does the combined chart get one level deeper.
limitations: Real mergers negotiate; here the rule is fixed.
Size-based merging compares headcount instead of depth.

steps.explanation: Each pair of equal rank-0 roots makes a rank-1 root.
Equal-rank roots are joined and the chosen new root's rank increases once.
The tree's height stays within log2 of its size.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing union by rank. Step 1, Pairs: roots is 0 (rank 1), 2 (rank 1). Each pair of equal rank-0 roots makes a rank-1 root. Step 2, Equal ranks: new root is 0; rank[0] is 2; parent[2] is 0. Equal-rank roots are joined and the chosen new root's rank increases once. Step 3, Height: height is 2; members is 4 = 2^2. The tree's height stays within log2 of its size.

remediation.explanation: At each union say: **"lower rank goes under; if equal, bump the new root's rank."** Update rank only for roots and only on ties.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The chain built by always attaching left".

recap.summary: To implement union by rank or size, attach the lower-rank (or smaller) root under the higher-rank (or larger) one, increase the new root's rank only when two equal ranks join, and keep representatives as roots, which bounds tree height by O(log n) and keeps find fast.
